editorial:
Imagine you are running from the law after a credit card scam and your only hope is a place to hide. That is exactly where Price finds himself. He takes a tip from his cousin and ducks into a college fraternity house to stay off the radar. The problem is, his cousin forgot to mention that every single guy in the house is gay. Now, Price has to fake his way through the experience and pretend he is part of the community just to keep his spot. It is a wild setup that leads to some really funny and awkward moments as he tries to keep his secret while several guys start falling for him.

You will love how the movie handles the chaos and the fast pacing. The acting is light and fun, making the misunderstandings feel natural. While it is a simple comedy, the heart of the story is about learning to be open-minded. If you are in the mood for a laugh, you should definitely look for this on streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick if you want something easygoing and silly to watch with friends.
endingExplained: By the end, Price cannot keep up the act anymore and finally comes clean about his identity and his legal troubles. Instead of kicking him out, the guys in the frat house support him because they have grown to truly care for him. Price learns a big lesson about love and acceptance. He manages to settle his legal issues and leaves the house as a much kinder, more open person than he was at the start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy mistaken identity comedies.
